patch.value: Fleet attribution analytics: per-harness and per-model throughput, rework, and defect-escape rates derived from immutable history alone

Once identity carries harness and model, the immutable history streams already contain everything needed to answer the questions a fleet operator actually has, with no new stored state and no telemetry: which model's work is reopened most often; which harness produces the most unresolved-validation warnings; how completion time distributes per model on comparable item types; which model's closes later attract a defect item linked by discovered_from; how much of a workspace's mutation volume is annotation versus state change per agent class. These are derivations over the same append-only streams that pm-pee5 uses for flow metrics, restricted and grouped by the provenance dimensions rather than by item. The output must be bounded and comparable: rates and distributions with sample counts, never raw per-entry dumps, and never a leaderboard that invites optimizing the metric. Explicitly out of scope: using these numbers as an authorization or routing input — detected identity is an unverified claim, and pm-3oqjnc owns allocation decisions on capability declarations, not on inferred quality scores.

Analytics are pure derivations over immutable history with no new stored state and no telemetry dependency; Grouping is available by harness, by model, and by author_source, and every reported figure carries its sample count and window; A metric with an insufficient sample is reported as insufficient rather than as a number, so small workspaces get honest output; Output is bounded by the same token-budget contract as other read surfaces and degrades deterministically instead of dumping entries; The documentation states that these figures are observational, that detected identity is unverified, and that the figures must not be used as an authorization or allocation input; A workspace with no model provenance (pre-capture history) produces correct harness-level output and reports the model dimension as unavailable rather than empty
A fleet operator can compare agent classes on evidence already recorded, without instrumenting anything
Thousands of concurrent agents of different models are the target deployment; without per-model attribution there is no way to tell an improving fleet from a degrading one
Adds derived read-only analytics over existing streams; introduces a real risk of metric-gaming that the acceptance criteria must bound
Model and harness selection for a workspace becomes an evidence-backed decision instead of a preference
